solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Being controversial male, I celebrate on perch

indicators.note: in an across answer, the pieces placed on the perch word come after it

parts.note: a perch for a bird can be a pole
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: A man in a boastful mood sings his own praises from a high perch and stirs up argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the male piece before the perch, but 'on' sends the rest to sit after it, as on a perch.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemics are controversial arguments, so engaging in them is being deliberately contentious.

clue.text: Quiet one heading naughty act to defraud author

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for playing quietly
I is the Roman numeral for one
racy means risqué or a bit naughty

explanation.surface: A soft-spoken person leads some mischief to cheat a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' just places P and I in front of RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Piracy is the unauthorised copying of a work, robbing its author of royalties.

clue.text: Possible description of foot in story?

definitions.meaning: the foot is the end of the leg

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a foot appears in a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional story handed down, and read as two words it describes the bottom of a limb.

clue.text: Holy pair maybe held at Richmond after disturbance?

indicators.note: after being disturbed, these letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Some sacred couple has been detained in a London suburb following a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmond is a town and borough in south-west London. 'maybe' marks the Madonna and Child as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virgin and the infant Jesus are the classic holy pairing in religious art.

clue.text: Win gold as the one taking over a mantle

definitions.text: the one taking over a mantle

parts.note: a win is a success
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gaining a gold medal casts a sportsperson as the heir to a great tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever takes over another's role or mantle is that person's heir in office.

clue.text: Bit of cotton in one type of fabric

indicators.note: only a bit of these words is wanted, a stretch running across them

explanation.surface: A scrap of cotton is found in one kind of material.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'cotton' through 'in' into the start of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninon is a sheer lightweight dress material, often silk or nylon, used for veils and curtains.

clue.text: Brave man tackled by the rogue

indicators.note: the answer is held, as if gripped in a tackle, within these words

explanation.surface: A courageous fellow is brought down by a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a person admired for courage, a brave man.

clue.text: Time that's black that can be removed from the record

definitions.text: that can be removed from the record

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sable is the heraldic word for black

explanation.surface: A dark period of history that could be struck from the books.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erasable can be rubbed out or deleted from a record.

clue.text: It could make one ever so zonked going round party!

definitions.text: It could make one ever so zonked going round party!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters surround the party word, split around it
zonked means stupefied, so the letters of these words are scrambled

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone warns that a party-goer may end up stupefied after taking too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zonked' looks like part of the picture of a drugged person, but it is the anagram signal; the whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking too much of a drug is an overdose, which could leave anyone stupefied.

clue.text: Accusing one with position in cricket involved in pilfering

indicators.note: one piece is involved within the other, placed inside it

parts.note: to finger something is slang for stealing it, so pilfering is fingering
point is a cricket fielding position, and the fielder there is also called point

explanation.surface: A cricketer is blamed for petty theft.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket fielders are named after where they stand, so the fielder at point is simply 'point'.
explanation.definitionFit: Finger-pointing is the act of blaming or accusing others.

clue.text: Orthodox and intelligent? Not bishop

indicators.note: not having the bishop means its letter is removed

parts.note: bright means clever or intelligent
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A conservative churchman is said to be traditional and clever, but no bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodox views are conventional ones, and right is used of views that are correct or conservative.

clue.text: Someone standing at back of house? Frank is at the front

indicators.note: the frank word is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: candid means frank and honest

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone stands behind the house while a man named Frank waits at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone who stands for election to an office.

clue.text: Gather nearly all the nuns before start of evensong

indicators.note: nearly all means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a convent is the community of nuns

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The sisters mostly assemble before the evening service begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' takes T off CONVENT to leave CONVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To convene is to gather or assemble for a meeting.

clue.text: Mean person trailin' around

indicators.note: around means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: trailing is dragging, here with its final g dropped to match

explanation.surface: A stingy person loafs about, dragging their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'trailin'' signals the dropped G, so the synonym is DRAGGIN'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a miser, a stingy or mean person.

clue.text: Seagull soars around for food

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A gull wheels about in the sky hunting for something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausage rolls are savoury pastry snacks, a common British food.

clue.text: Manages to fill the top post and grows stronger

definitions.text: Manages to fill the top post
definitions.meaning: an organisation that recruits a head for its top post ...
to advance or move forward, get further on

explanation.surface: A school finally appoints a headteacher and goes from strength to strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting ahead means making progress, and split differently it describes obtaining a new head.

clue.text: Monsieur is leader in funny business

parts.note: a chief is a leader

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is in charge of some comic goings-on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is playful misbehaviour, the sort of thing called funny business.

clue.text: Son to go off and smoke

parts.note: to moulder is to decay or rot, to go off

explanation.surface: A father tells his son to leave and have a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To smoulder is to burn slowly giving off smoke.

clue.text: I am having the means, given allowance in excess

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
a mode is a means or method
a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: Someone with the money, once given an allowance, indulges too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoderation is lack of restraint, indulging to excess.

clue.text: Like ships making attack

parts.note: as means like
sail is used collectively for ships, as in a fleet of forty sail

explanation.surface: Vessels in formation prepare for an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack violently.

clue.text: Only just see obstacle above

indicators.note: in a down answer, above puts one piece on top of the next

parts.note: a bar is an obstacle
Ely is a cathedral city and its bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone can barely see past a barrier above them.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; ELY is the crossword's favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Barely means scarcely, by the narrowest margin, only just.

clue.text: A hundred ran — injured in stampede?

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
rushed means ran quickly

explanation.surface: A hundred people bolt and someone is hurt in the stampede.
explanation.definitionFit: Being crushed is the typical injury of someone caught in a stampede, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Benefactor has name inscribed in entrance

indicators.note: written into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A patron has their name carved over the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is someone who gives money, a benefactor.

clue.text: Supposed condition of legionnaire or seaman, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, so the letters are unreliable and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor wonders whether a soldier or he himself suffers from some condition.
explanation.walkthrough: Men were said to join the French Foreign Legion to forget their past.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, the condition legionnaires reputedly sought.

clue.text: Lack of energy could make for decline, no?

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into another word

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being lazy leads to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolence is laziness, a lack of energy or effort.

clue.text: Picture that is wrapped around outside of periodical

indicators.note: one piece is wrapped round the outside of another, which goes inside

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
a mag is a periodical, short for magazine

explanation.surface: A photo is wrapped round the cover of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: An absurdity not having cold food

indicators.note: not having means the letter is left out

parts.note: a farce is an absurdity
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: It is ridiculous that the meal is not cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is food and drink, as in simple country fare.

clue.text: Irresponsibly makes professional sneer against friend

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a dig is a sneering remark
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A professional makes cutting remarks about a friend in a careless way.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting prodigally means spending wastefully, which is irresponsible.
